newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea to detail individual bank ownership limit.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea to detail individual bank ownership limit.

text.p: South Korea's finance and economy ministry plans to make an announcement this week concerning the individual bank ownership ceiling, a ministry official said on Monday.
"We have already unveiled government proposals on financial reform. But we did not specifically mention bank ownership, which will be released this week," the official said.
The official declined to give details of ministry officials' discussions or the date on which the government would make its announcement.

The Naeway Economic Daily said on Monday afternoon the government would expand the ceiling to 15 percent from current four percent. It also said the ministry would allow big conglomerates, or chaebols, to jointly own and run commercial banks.
The ministry unveiled on June 16 its final financial reform proposals, which were preceded by a draft from the Presidential Commission for Financial Reform.

The ministry's proposals said the three existing supervisory bodies for the banking, securities and insurance sectors would be integrated into a unified organisation under the authority of the prime minister.
But union workers at the watchdog agencies have vowed to go on strike unless the government drops the plan to unify the three bodies.
